summary: Members of this build advertise message_view_reads, so a fleet whose members all run it records each seat's delivery, read and close as marks on the seat's host; a fault's target states and work wakes ask that host as message views do, and a host's answer never feeds a client message's revision (db break-up step 4b, the views, part 2)

replay.detail: Once every other member advertises message_view_reads=1, which this build is the first to do, a member writes no message.delivered, message.read or message.closed claim for a seat its own declarations place on it, as a member alone already did: it records a local mark, which never replicates, and other members ask it. Stagings stay message.staged claims. Lifecycle claims already written keep counting.

rules.detail: daemon.started advertises message_view_reads=1, so the 4b-2 barrier (every other current member, and every configured peer, advertises it) holds in a fleet of this build. A fault's target_states for mail to a seat on such a host, and a work wake's acknowledged_by in GET /v1/work-items, /v1/work, /v1/mission-runs and the client's mission detail, ask that host within a second, as message views do: read or closed acknowledges a wake as consumed, delivered as delivery while the assignee works in the wake's incarnation, and a claim still wins. They are patched when served, after the page cache and its digest: a host's answer never feeds a revision, and a client sees it on its next read. A client message resource keeps this member's own revision and updated_at, which part 1 raised from the host's newest mark. Known limit (#4866): the client message selector's history layer and reminder winner still count only this member's closes, so mail the seat's host closed leaves the current list but does not reach history until a close arrives here.

compatibility.detail: A member of v0.3.25 or earlier, or of a build before this one, advertises no message_view_reads, so a fleet with one keeps writing lifecycle claims exactly as before, and every member reads every seat's lifecycle as before. In a fleet of this build only, another member's seat's mail reads from its host: in delivery status, doctor and the mail backlog (v0.3.25 on), and in message views, lists, fault targets and wakes (this build). No request or response shape changes; status_from is as in part 1.

downtime.detail: No migration: marks start with the next lifecycle write once every member runs this build and the barrier holds, decided at startup and every minute.

manual.detail: No operator steps. doctor's message-marks check shows the decision and names any member that has not advertised message_view_reads.

recovery.detail: Rolling one member back to an earlier build turns marks off on every member within a minute, and each writes claims from then on. Marks already recorded stay where they are. The rolled-back member reads its own seats' marks (v0.3.25 on). It reads another host's seats' marks only in delivery status, doctor and the mail backlog. Its message views, lists, fault targets and wakes show that mail as far as its last claim, often sent, until the seat's next lifecycle write after marks turn off, which is a claim. Nothing is redelivered: a seat's own host keeps its marks and offers nothing again. Rolling back to v0.3.24 or earlier is as the 4b-2 note says.
